executiveSummary: GM0050 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but it is not a calibrated Zeewolde first-72-hour forecast. Official evidence describes a large, sparsely populated Flevoland municipality below NAP, with the core and rural/nature areas connected to the Hoge Vaart system, continual seepage and cross-boundary pumping; distinct Wolderwijd/Nuldernauw outer-dike and primary-defence pathways; and one of the country's largest contiguous deciduous forests beside the town. The adopted Flevoland fire-coverage plan specifically flags nature-fire proximity to Zeewolde, distant firefighting water, overnight recreation, access/knowledge gaps and lack of specialised equipment. The model instead produces an unnamed river legacy flood amplitude of 0.857446 through T+72, exact service/recovery percentages, and one identical full neighbourhood order for eight unrelated single hazards plus compound. Canonical wildfire has zero direct fire and synthetic smoke, so it does not exercise the priority Horsterwold pathway. Static water assets, roads, grid planning, antennas, schools and external hospitals add useful context but not live topology, state, capacity, access or recovery. Missing and out-of-coverage values remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0050 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG place and neighbourhoods
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS table identifies GM0050 as Zeewolde and reports 24,291 residents, density 98 per square kilometre, 16.4% aged 65 or older and 3,459 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The generated reference point [5.461973275468764, 52.344826558983144] and the single active BAG place point, Zeewolde, lie inside the 2025 generalized boundary. BRT provides two woonkernen, Zeewolde and Harderhaven; the different registers have different settlement ontologies.

Eleven neighbourhood rows sum to 24,290 residents, one below the municipal total (-0.004%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 24,291. Official zero residents in Buurt 5 and Horstenparc remain zero, while their registered business/building activity must be modelled separately from residents.

evidenceSources.title: NWB corridors, cross-water structures, rail absence and scheduled public transport
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026 under CC0; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; official structure/current road pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Monthly NWB generates ten logical boundary links to Almere, Lelystad, Dronten, Nijkerk and Harderwijk over A6, A27, N301, N302, N305, N306 and N706. N302, N305 and N706 occur on multiple municipal sides and are series/shared physical corridors, not additive independent capacity.

The reference-town route toward 24/7 acute care in Harderwijk uses the N302 cross-water system. Rijkswaterstaat documents that the Veluwemeer connection combines a fixed bridge and aqueduct; static geometry is not event-time passability, emergency priority or throughput.

A6/A27 boundary contacts do not by themselves prove direct town access. No ProRail station lies inside GM0050 and 36 GTFS stop areas are assigned, including Harderhaven and rural/recreation stops. Geometry and schedules do not establish current bus, bridge, aqueduct, road or destination operation.
The bounded deployment has no GM0050 NDW situation, camera or transport-restriction record. That is time/coverage output, not an all-open assertion.

evidenceSources.title: 2022 climate stress test, Waterbuurt measures and public crisis guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal retrospective published 2026; current project and crisis pages inspected 3 September 2026; no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: The municipality says its 2022 climate stress test identified the Waterlinie, Ossenkampweg, shopping centre and Corridor as vulnerable to water nuisance, drought or heat, with measures phased in 2025–2028. This is planning/stress-test evidence, not a live event surface or completed protection.

Waterbuurt design material identifies water-on-street in a one-in-ten-year rainfall case and proposes seven local surface-flow interventions toward open water and lower green space. Native rainfall, terrain, sewer assumptions, model edition, resolution, licence and NoData are needed before analytical use.

The official crisis page at https://www.zeewolde.nl/ramp-of-crisis describes warning, shelter-in-place, regional broadcasting, neighbour checks and evacuation for threats including flooding. It links preparedness guidance but does not prove notification reach, household stock, evacuation routes, reception capacity or completed actions.

The municipal retrospective also says the electricity network is filling and identifies a business energy collective at Horsterparc-Trekkersveld. Long-horizon policy and collaboration are not incident-time grid state.

evidenceSources.title: Hoge Vaart and Lovink pumping, Wolderwijd exposure and public Zeewolde water assets
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-board/RWS pages; Hoge Vaart/Zuidlob peilbesluit 2017; outer-dike harbour inventory 2014; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Zuiderzeeland says Lovink pumps the Hoge division of eastern/southern Flevoland about four metres upward into the Veluwemeer even without rain because seepage continues. Published targets are -6.20 m NAP for Lage Vaart and -5.20 m NAP for Hoge Vaart; two Lovink pumps each have stated capacity 550 cubic metres per minute and start automatically on high level. These facts do not establish current operation, available capacity, power, maintenance or backup.

The 2017 peilbesluit covers urban Zeewolde and surrounding nature/agriculture within a roughly 25,000-hectare, 35-compartment system, with water levels around -3.00 to -5.20 m NAP and excess discharged by several cross-boundary pumping stations. It is static control/design evidence, not a flood observation.

Rijkswaterstaat identifies Wolderwijd as an 18-square-kilometre randmeer and exposes current water/bridge/sluice information routes. A 2014 Zuiderzeeland inventory separately describes a 19-hectare outer-dike Haven Zeewolde area with homes/harbour, 26 embankment sections and a 1/10 norm beside Wolderwijd. This dated inventory must not be generalized to the protected polder or treated as current defence state.

The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH collections contain 119 GM0050 context points: 30 sewer pumps, 3 sluices, 5 surface-water pumps, 1 wastewater treatment point and 80 weirs. Capacity is null for 99; remaining values lack comparable units/topology/state and cannot be summed as emergency capacity.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024 and Dekkingsplan Flevoland 2025–2028
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive RRP 2024 and coverage plan adopted 11 December 2024; official policy/scenario evidence, no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: The regional profile notes that almost all Flevoland lies below NAP, water management assets are essential, and climate change intensifies extreme-weather, flood, nature-fire and vital-infrastructure risks. Flooding, storm/rain, cold, heat, electricity, voice/data, cyberattack and nature fire are priority risks; this supports the preset set but not its local numeric calibration.

The adopted fire coverage plan explicitly identifies nature-area proximity to the Zeewolde town, firefighting water at excessive distance, weak access/area knowledge and planning, extensive overnight recreation on the province's east side and lack of specialised nature-fire equipment as risk/control gaps.

The plan schedules coordination, prevention, area plans, a Flevoland fire handbook, basic competence and an updated risk index through 2028. Planned measures are not live suppression resources or guaranteed containment.

Regional profiles are strategic expert-judgement products. They do not provide an incident ignition, perimeter, fuel moisture, wind/plume, people present, road closure, water source, crew or T+72 action state.

evidenceSources.title: Horsterwold extent, access and current recreation-infrastructure limitations
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages inspected 3 September 2026; access/closure notice 20 November 2025; no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: Staatsbosbeheer describes Horsterwold as one of the largest contiguous deciduous forests in the Netherlands, with an extensive path network, less-accessible interior areas and walking, cycling, horse, canoe, camping and organised recreation.

A 2025 notice says deteriorated bridges and cycle paths in Horsterwold/Hulkesteinse Bos are increasingly closed for safety, with signed detours. Current notices establish access constraints for visitors, not fire-engine passability or an emergency routing graph.

Forest extent and recreation establish eligible fuel, smoke, evacuation and non-resident exposure domains. They do not establish ignition, fuel moisture, flame front, smoke plume, event-time visitors, closures, firefighting water, resources or containment.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / Ziekenhuis St Jansdal
evidenceSources.title: Public grid-planning, communications, education and cross-boundary acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public planning/register snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; hospital pages current on 3 September 2026
supports: One postcode sample, 3893EB, maps to Liander OS ZEEWOLDE 10-1i: withdrawal existing/required/queued 42/30/8.8 MW with 31 requests; injection 42/34/31 MW with 22 requests; 27 projects and earliest year 2030. It is planning at one sample, not municipal coverage, live load, outage, switching or restoration; the exact dataset reuse licence was not identified.

RDI returns 87 antenna sites: 42 mobile, 25 fixed-link, 17 amateur, 2 broadcast and 1 other-mobile. DUO returns 18 education records: 9 primary, 1 secondary, 1 special and 7 other. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, occupants, shelter role, supplies or current operation; RDI cadence/licence is unstated and DUO is daily under CC Attribution version unspecified.

RIVM's annual CC0 v1.1 questionnaire assigns no full emergency department to GM0050. St Jansdal says its Zeewolde location provides only blood collection and radiology, while Harderwijk provides regional 24/7 emergency, intensive, cardiac and acute obstetric care.

Straight-line reference-point distances are 10.474 km to St Jansdal Harderwijk, 16.432 km to Flevoziekenhuis Almere and 20.299 km to Meander Amersfoort. These are not ambulance times, route availability, live acceptance, staffing, occupancy, backup duration or restoration.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM0050 is uniquely Zeewolde in Flevoland and Veiligheidsregio Flevoland.
The reference point is inside the 2025 generalized geometry and no headline mismatch was found.
Annual statistics, static plans/registers, current web pages and the synthetic exercise clock retain separate valid times.

geography.summary: The municipal geometry is coherent, but polder, randmeer, defence and forest pathways require full source geometry.
notes: One district and 11 neighbourhoods cover a very large mix of town, polder agriculture, business sites, forest and water-edge land.
Hoge Vaart compartments and pumps, Wolderwijd/Nuldernauw outer-dike and primary-defence zones, and Horsterwold cross neighbourhood and municipal/network boundaries.
A municipal scalar, centre distance or shared rank cannot replace event-specific connected flood, fire/spread/plume and exposure geometry.
Every analytical layer needs publisher, edition, scenario, CRS/resolution, licence, coverage and NoData.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and the one-person rounding difference is explicit.
notes: Population 24,291, density 98, age65Pct 16.4 and one-person households 3,459 agree.
Neighbourhood populations sum to 24,290 (-1, -0.004%); generated allocation reconciles exactly. Published households sum to 10,505 and age65+ rows to 3,990.
Largest neighbourhoods are Derde woonwijk 6,085, Buurt 4 5,830, Tweede woonwijk 4,750 and Eerste woonwijk 3,495.
Residents exclude campers, forest/water recreation, commuters, pupils, care users, workers and responders; official zero-resident business areas can have separate activity demand.

regionalDetail.summary: All neighbourhoods load, but socioeconomic, hydraulic and operational coverage is incomplete.
notes: Home value, household size, density, tenure, housing type, doctor/supermarket distance and most benefits cover 9/11; cars per household 8/11; district heating and public charging 0/11. Null is not zero.
Of 119 local HWH water points, 99 capacities are null; non-null values are not comparable system capacity without native units, connectivity and state.
One grid-planning sample, 87 antennas and 18 education records do not establish municipality-wide or incident-time service.

settlements.summary: Zeewolde and Harderhaven are coherent labels but arise from different settlement registers and do not quantify event occupancy.
notes: BAG provides one active woonplaats, Zeewolde, while BRT identifies Zeewolde and Harderhaven as woonkernen; no label-point boundary mismatch occurs.
Harderhaven, outer-dike harbour/recreation and rural/nature users require separate exposure evidence, not reassignment of CBS residents.
Missing event-time population, warning reach, shelter or supply role remains Unknown.

transport.summary: Ten logical boundary links are reproducible but overstate independent access and omit critical structures and destinations.
notes: Ten links represent seven named physical corridors; repeated N302/N305/N706 sections are non-additive and A6/A27 boundary contacts are not direct town-route guarantees.
N302 and its Veluwemeer bridge/aqueduct are central to Harderwijk acute care. Internal rural/forest roads, bridges, detours and event passability are unresolved.
No local station and 36 scheduled stops do not establish operation. Empty NDW/camera/restriction screens are coverage, not all-open state.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities, warnings and priority hazards are documented, but no auditable local first-72-hour action/resource state exists.
notes: Municipality, VRF, Zuiderzeeland, Rijkswaterstaat, province, Staatsbosbeheer, utilities, ambulance/GHOR and external hospitals have distinct roles not represented as triggers, assignments, resources, status or completion.
Nature-fire planning gaps and dispersed campers/visitors require source-aware warning, access, evacuation/shelter, firefighting water and welfare actions.
No full emergency department is local; Harderwijk/Almere continuity depends on ambulance, bridge/aqueduct/road, live acceptance, staff and utilities that remain Unknown.
Preparedness and evacuation guidance are not measured household stock, operating support points or T+72 recovery.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: The mandatory gate covers all ten presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Affected people-equivalent is not observed people, casualties or evacuees; person-hours is cumulative weighted local service shortfall against a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0050 pnpm audit:model passed both tests over the complete matrix.
Zero-event effects, repeatability, UI/core preset equality, local population/demand/delivery, route ceilings, hazard-layer invariance and burden monotonicity pass.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local physical or operational calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic river forcing and one repeated local order do not follow Zeewolde's defence, drainage, heat or forest mechanisms.
notes: River T+24/T+72 reports legacy amplitude 0.857446 and unchanged severity 0.266249 without a selected randmeer level, primary-defence breach, compartment/control state or connected footprint.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire use the identical full T+24 order: Tweede woonwijk, Knardijkgebied, Centrum, Horstenparc, Eerste woonwijk, Trekkersveld, Zuidlob, Buurt 4, Buurt 5, Derde woonwijk, Middengebied. Compound repeats it.
Official stress-test attention to Waterlinie, Ossenkampweg, Centrum and Corridor cannot be evaluated from that rank, and Horsterwold extent/ignition/spread is absent.
Official zero-resident Horstenparc ranks fourth for every active hazard; business activity may be material but cannot substitute for resident exposure or hazard-specific geography.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service values are inspectable but unsupported by water, utility, route, fire or acute-care evidence.
notes: Compound T+24 availability is power 0.409751, water 0.440320, drainage 0.299781, gas 0.621272, telecom 0.296939, mobility 0.850166, facilities 0.389624 and supply 0.842648; no operator validates these values.
HWH points, one NBNL sample, antennas, schools, NWB geometry and hospital registers remain non-causal context.
Lovink/Hoge Vaart operation, bridge/aqueduct access, firefighting water, telecom backhaul and external-hospital acceptance/backup are missing.
Unavailable or security-sensitive topology requires an explicit aggregate synthetic fallback, not asset-looking precision.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes exist, but unresolved flood, fire, cyber and operational dimensions are not exposed.
notes: River shows exact local inundation without source lake/river, boundary water level/hydrograph, datum, wind, defence/breach, compartment, footprint, arrival or recession.
Canonical wildfire is an external synthetic smoke case with direct fire zero; it cannot be presented as a test of Horsterwold ignition, spread or containment. Cyber lacks a named target/dependency.
A legacy field named floodDepthM must not be displayed as surveyed or forecast metres.
Current pages, dated inventories/peilbesluit, long-horizon projects, public registers and synthetic T+72 output require distinct issue/valid time and evidence class.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood/compound plateaus and exact recovery elsewhere lack first-72-hour actions and resources.
notes: River severity and flood amplitude stay exactly fixed T+24–72, seven services stay fixed, Facilities falls 0.700177 to 0.552075, affected rises 5,611 to 6,320 and person-hours reach 552,997.805 without pump, dewatering, evacuation or repair state.
Compound T+72 keeps flood amplitude 0.212666, pressure about 0.487, affected 11,876 and virtually the exact T+24 eight-service plateau while person-hours reach 826,452.842.

Storm/pluvial/winter/wildfire direct forcing clears and cyber declines with exact residual services; heat severity stays 0.115876 but affected falls to zero. Coastal/earthquake have no direct flood/shaking at T+24 yet accumulate 52,103.328 and 29,273.275 person-hours by T+72.
No warning, evacuation/shelter, pump/defence action, fire containment, road clearance, hospital acceptance, utility crew, fuel, stock or mutual-aid evidence explains those trajectories.

findings.summary: Persistent generic river flooding lacks a selected randmeer, defence or Flevoland polder case.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 both report severity 0.266249 and legacy flood amplitude 0.857446; affected rises 5,611 to 6,320. Official evidence distinguishes Wolderwijd outer-dike harbour exposure, primary-defence failure and Hoge Vaart/pump/compartment processes, but the run selects no source water, boundary condition, dike section/failure, compartment/control state, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Suppress unsupported direct river precision. Enable inundation only through an expert-selected, versioned Zuiderzeeland/RWS/WMCN/LIWO case with source, boundary hydrograph/level and datum, defence/breach, compartment/control, footprint, depth/velocity, arrival/recession, probability, CRS/resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. Keep outer-dike, primary-defence and pluvial/polder cases separate.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated single hazards plus compound reuse one complete 11-neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire identically rank Tweede woonwijk, Knardijkgebied, Centrum, Horstenparc and Eerste woonwijk first. Compound repeats the full order. This cannot simultaneously encode defence breach, street flow, heat, wind, cyber target and Horsterwold fire/smoke; zero-resident Horstenparc is fourth under every active hazard.
findings.action: Replace the common municipality seed with hazard-specific source, eligible-domain, forcing and exposed-object adapters over full polygons. Add cross-preset rank-diversity tests; preserve zero residents while modelling business/visitor activity separately, and render unsupported spatial allocation Unknown rather than precise.

findings.summary: The wildfire preset does not exercise Zeewolde's priority Horsterwold fire pathway.
findings.evidence: Canonical wildfire T+24 has direct fire zero, synthetic smoke 0.438906, zero affected and 42,939.707 person-hours using the common rank. VRF identifies town/forest proximity, distant firefighting water, overnight recreation, access/knowledge/plan gaps and no specialised nature-fire equipment; Staatsbosbeheer establishes a large, partly less-accessible recreational forest. No ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind/plume, visitor/camper presence, access, water, crew or containment drives the run.
findings.action: Add a selectable Horsterwold case driven by versioned forest/fuel/reed land cover, explicit ignition/perimeter or labelled external plume, event-valid wind/moisture/spread, presence ranges, closure/access, firefighting water and suppression state. Missing source means no selected event/Unknown, not zero local risk or observed smoke.

findings.summary: Pluvial and drainage precision ignores official street-flow and cross-boundary polder pumping.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports legacy amplitude 0.205228 and Drainage 0.625331 without rainfall hyetograph, AHN/street flow, sewer-included flag, saturation, Hoge Vaart/compartment level, pump state, power or receiving Veluwemeer level. Official local evidence identifies Waterlinie/Ossenkampweg/Centrum/Corridor and seven Waterbuurt interventions, while Zuiderzeeland documents continuous seepage and cross-boundary Lovink pumping.
findings.action: Integrate the native municipal stress surface and Zuiderzeeland control case with rainfall, AHN/BGT, sewer/street/storage assumptions, groundwater/seepage, compartment/receiving levels, pump connectivity/state, units, edition, licence, resolution and NoData. Do not convert design or registry capacity to live availability.

findings.summary: Exact utility, firewater and recovery percentages have no operator evidence.
findings.evidence: Compound T+24 emits eight exact values from Telecom 0.296939 to Mobility 0.850166. The 119 water points, one Liander planning sample, 87 antennas, 18 schools and road/hospital registers provide no feeder/customer or pipe topology, comparable capacity, live load/pressure/backhaul, damage, priority users, backup, switching, firewater, crews or restoration commitments.
findings.action: Keep public context affectsSimulation=false and label operational states aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Integrate authorized time-scoped operator/authority aggregates where safe; otherwise use versioned aggregate zones/ranges and preserve manual override author, timestamp, scope and expiry.

findings.summary: Zeewolde's external acute-care dependency is reduced to a generic Facilities scalar.
findings.evidence: The local St Jansdal site offers blood collection/radiology, not full emergency care. RIVM identifies the nearest 24/7 SEHs in Harderwijk and Almere; the Harderwijk route depends on N302 and the Veluwemeer bridge/aqueduct. Straight-line distance and registered opening do not establish ambulance time, passability, diversion, staffing, occupancy, backup utilities or acceptance.
findings.action: Represent local outpatient role and external ED/obstetric/IC destination, live acceptance/diversion, ambulance and bridge/aqueduct route, backup/fuel and critical supply state only through authorized time-scoped evidence; absent fields remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Ten logical edges overstate independent connectivity and omit route structures and rural/forest access.
findings.evidence: N302/N305/N706 appear in multiple boundary records and A6/A27 make short boundary contacts, while the simulation has no full internal access graph, bridge/aqueduct state, forest closures, bus operation or destination acceptance. No bounded NDW/camera/restriction record is assigned.
findings.action: Retain NWB only for mobility/supply with physical-corridor and non-additive semantics. Add official structure, direction/mode, live restriction and destination state; empty feeds and missing internal routes render Unknown, not open or zero delay.

findings.summary: Static plans, dated scenarios, registers and synthetic trajectories need adjacent provenance and Unknown gates.
findings.evidence: The UI can juxtapose the 2014 harbour inventory, 2017 peilbesluit, 2022 stress test, 2025–2028 fire plan, current web pages, planning/register snapshots and exact T+72 output. River precision lacks its event dimensions, wildfire lacks a local source, cyber lacks a target, and empty local observations can be mistaken for normality.
findings.action: Attach publisher, dataset/version, retrieval, issue/valid/event time, evidence class, lifecycle, licence, coverage, spatial support, uncertainty, affectsSimulation and NoData to every layer/value/export. A normalized legacy flood field is never labelled measured depth/metres.

findings.summary: First-72-hour plateaus and recovery have no auditable actions, constraints or resources.
findings.evidence: River holds severity/depth and seven services fixed while affected grows and Facilities worsens; compound holds almost all service values through T+72. Other hazards clear or decline with exact residuals, and heat still has severity but zero affected. No authority/action/resource ledger represents warning, evacuation, pumps/defences, fire containment, road clearance, care acceptance, utility crews, fuel, stocks or mutual aid.
findings.action: Require checkpointed incident/action/resource records with authority/owner, target, trigger, prerequisite, route, crew/material/fuel/water, start/end, state, observation/valid time and uncertainty. Every deterioration, plateau, residual and recovery must cite a driver; absent state remains Unknown.

corrections.summary: Suppress generic GM0050 river precision and implement selected randmeer, primary-defence, outer-dike and polder cases.
corrections.validation: Without a compatible expert-selected case, GM0050 direct flooding is Unknown/unsupported rather than 0.857446. Fixtures retain source water, boundary level/hydrograph/datum, defence/breach, compartment/control, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival/recession, probability, CRS/resolution, licence, coverage and NoData; stress is never presented as metres.

corrections.summary: Replace the common GM0050 rank with hazard-aware local allocation and a selectable Horsterwold fire case.
corrections.validation: Eight unrelated single hazards plus compound cannot silently share all 11 ranks. Fire fixtures follow ignition/perimeter, full forest/fuel polygons, wind/moisture/spread and exposed-presence ranges; official zero residents remain zero while activity demand is separate.

corrections.summary: Integrate Zeewolde stress-test and Zuiderzeeland polder/pump dependencies without promoting plans or registry values to operation.
corrections.validation: Pluvial cases retain rainfall, street/storage/sewer assumptions, terrain, seepage, compartment/receiving level, pump connectivity/state, power, units, edition, licence and NoData. Ninety-nine null asset capacities and published design figures remain Unknown/non-operational.

corrections.summary: Add physical-corridor, structure and destination semantics for Zeewolde access and external acute care.
corrections.validation: Repeated route sections remain non-additive; A6/A27 boundary contacts do not imply town access; N302 bridge/aqueduct, rural/forest approaches, bus state and Harderwijk/Almere care destinations show time-scoped passability/acceptance or explicit Unknown.

corrections.summary: Evidence-gate lifelines and implement an Unknown-first first-72-hour action/resource ledger.
corrections.validation: Every service, warning, evacuation, water/defence, fire, transport, care, reception/resupply and repair state has compatible provenance/valid time and owner/action/resource/constraint or is labelled synthetic/Unknown; only confirmed actions affect recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, care, firefighting-water or supply topology, live control state, backup endurance, crews, stocks or restoration estimates.

No selected RWS/Zuiderzeeland/WMCN/LIWO case establishes a GM0050 randmeer level, primary-defence breach, compartment/control state, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. No selected case is not a safety finding.
The 2022 municipal climate stress test and Waterbuurt designs need native machine layers, event assumptions, CRS/resolution, units, licence, lifecycle and NoData before analytical use.
HWH's 119 heterogeneous objects contain 99 null capacities and no complete hydraulic/sewer/defence topology, settings, power, maintenance, backup or live state.
Horsterwold extent and VRF policy establish eligibility and response concerns but not ignition, fuel moisture, plume, visitors/campers, access, firefighting water, crews or containment.

Ten NWB links, no local rail, 36 scheduled stops and empty NDW/camera/restriction screens do not establish scenario-time operation, passability, vehicle eligibility, detours, emergency priority, destination or throughput.

St Jansdal/RIVM records do not expose ambulance availability, external ED acceptance/diversion, staffing, occupancy, critical utilities, backup or restoration; protected operational information must not be inferred.
CBS residents omit campers, forest/water visitors, commuters, workers, pupils, care users, volunteers and responders; business/building proxies do not identify event presence.
One Liander planning sample is not municipal coverage or outage evidence, and sensitive topology must not be reconstructed publicly.
Current weather, water, warning, road and facility state can change after completion; missing or stale observations/forecasts must degrade to Unknown, not be held constant or interpreted as zero.

Exact hazard, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercises, not observations, forecasts, operator commitments or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the case.
This audit covers only 72 hours; pumping/dewatering, agricultural/nature impacts, displaced care and infrastructure restoration can persist much longer.
provinceReviewFlags: Flevoland, VRF, Zuiderzeeland and Rijkswaterstaat should define expert selection/versioning for randmeer primary-defence breach, outer-dike and polder/pluvial cases, including compartment/control, footprint, units, arrival/recession, uncertainty and NoData.

VRF, Staatsbosbeheer, province and Zeewolde should review full-polygon Horsterwold/Hulkesteinse fire and smoke cases with ignition, fuel/moisture, wind, visitors/campers, closure/access, firefighting water, resources and first-72-hour tactics.

Zuiderzeeland and municipalities should review privacy-safe Hoge/Lage Vaart, Lovink/other pumping, sewer/street/storage and power/manual dependencies without exposing sensitive topology or treating registry capacity as live.

Province, Rijkswaterstaat, municipalities, transit and care partners should review A6/A27/N301/N302/N305/N306/N706 and cross-water structures as physical, non-additive, valid-time evacuation/fire/care/supply/repair routes.

Flevoland partners should turn preparedness into typed activation-gated warning, evacuation/shelter, nature-fire, medical, utility, drainage, food/water/fuel and recovery actions, separating plan, observation, forecast, official scenario, live state, synthetic assumption and Unknown.
